name: Critical minerals
summary: China extended its pause on some rare-earth export controls to 10 Jan 2027 on 9 Nov; April 2025 licensing stays
state: On 9 Nov China's commerce ministry extended its suspension of some rare-earth export controls, due to end on 10 Nov, to 10 Jan 2027 (S&P Global). Licensing requirements imposed in April 2025 on seven heavy rare earths, including dysprosium and terbium, remain in force. Searches on 19 Nov found no new controls and no production stoppages outside China linked to export bans, so Watch holds.
for_you: Mainly affects manufacturers of magnets, electric vehicles, wind turbines and defence equipment that rely on Chinese heavy rare earths. The pause defers rather than removes the risk of tighter supply.
rubric_hit: Watch: export licensing on heavy rare earths still in force; no reported production stoppages outside China (Alert)

sources.title: S&P Global Commodity Insights — China extends rare earth export suspension to January 2027

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
